title: A forced 1.924 m/s outer-orbit third harmonic raises fit error in 207 GJ 3293 velocities with three inner circular orbits
abstract: We test whether an eccentric outer planet can account for a near-41-day residual in 207 public HARPS velocities of GJ 3293. Three inner orbits are circular at published periods. The outer period is fixed or free from 120 to 125 days. The free-period fit gives a third harmonic of 0.087 m/s. A separate 41.135236-day term still has amplitude 1.887 m/s and lowers weighted squared error from 151.054 to 129.280. A direct physical third-harmonic constraint of 1.924 m/s gives best error 208.926. This is 57.872 above the free orbit. Eight phase starts per eccentricity and 80 starts for the main constrained case check local fit stability. The result disfavors a simple outer-harmonic explanation within this model. It does not detect a planet or identify the residual cause. The data and selected frequency are shared with prior campaign work. Correlated errors, fixed inner periods, circular inner orbits, and no independent instrument test limit the result. The package contains code, aggregate profiles, figures, provenance, and an external-source retrieval script. External source records are excluded from the baseline publication.

display.caption: Physical outer-orbit fits with three inner circular orbits. Left: eccentricity profiles with and without the fixed extra wave. Right: the direct third-harmonic amplitude constraint. Weighted error is relative to the free-period outer-only minimum. These are fit diagnostics, not significance curves.

citations.reason: Supplies the selected residual period and early amplitude. We directly test its proposed outer-harmonic confusion.
Earlier exact-orbit controls motivate our direct harmonic constraint. This study shares the published velocities and is not independent confirmation.
Related tests show model and reduction limits for a weak known inner wave.
